place.source_title: Herbert and Katherine Jacobs House I, Toepfer & Birch Avenues, Westmorland

brief: Wright's first Usonian house (1937), an L-shaped one-storey house of horizontal board-and-batten wood and brick piers under very low flat roofs with broad overhangs and a band of clerestory windows, a brick chimney mass at the core and a carport, screened from the street by a planted prairie border in a 1930s-50s subdivision.

floors: W W W W W W W
facade.notes: the Jacobs House I (Madison, 1937), Wright's first Usonian: a long low wall of horizontal board-and-batten and brick piers under a thin flat roof with deep overhangs, a clerestory band of windows, a carport at one end; the street front almost blind; a native prairie garden of asters and grasses in front

why.note: Wright's Usonian house (1936-59): an affordable flat-roofed L on a slab, built of a few materials, turned from the street toward a garden
a prairie planting instead of a lawn: the house's garden faces the back, the street gets grasses
